# Activity: Data Intake Card {.unnumbered}

## Goal

Students practice evaluating whether a health dataset is usable, ethical, documented, and appropriate for reproducible analysis.

## Approved Starter Portals

Choose **one** dataset or indicator page from one of the portals below.

1. **Survey-style microdata:** NHANES or NHIS from CDC/NCHS.
2. **Aggregated indicators:** WHO Global Health Observatory.
3. **Canadian open data:** BC Data Catalogue or the Open Government Portal.

The NHANES Health Equity data spine can be used as the shared practice example when students need a common dataset.

## Student Template

```yaml
dataset_name: ""
publisher_org: ""
permalink_url: ""
date_accessed: "YYYY-MM-DD"
license_terms: ""
geography: ""
time_coverage: ""
data_level: ""   # microdata / aggregated / unknown
variables_of_interest:
  - name: ""
    definition: ""
known_limitations:
  - ""
stewardship_notes: ""
ai_use_note: ""
```

## Completed Example: NHANES

```yaml
dataset_name: "NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset"
publisher_org: "CDC / National Center for Health Statistics"
permalink_url: "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/"
date_accessed: "YYYY-MM-DD"
license_terms: "Public-use NHANES files; cite CDC/NCHS documentation"
geography: "United States"
time_coverage: "Multiple NHANES cycles represented in the prepared class file"
data_level: "Microdata-derived classroom dataset"
variables_of_interest:
  - name: "BMI"
    definition: "Body mass index from NHANES body measures data"
known_limitations:
  - "Prepared class dataset is descriptive and should not be treated as a causal analysis"
  - "Population inference requires attention to NHANES survey design and weights"
stewardship_notes: "Use public-use data responsibly, avoid small-cell disclosure, and state limitations plainly."
ai_use_note: "AI may help draft plain-language summaries, but source documentation must be checked directly."
```

## Completion Checklist

To be marked **Complete**, your card must include:

- [ ] A stable link or access date.
- [ ] Publisher or organization.
- [ ] License or terms of use.
- [ ] Data level: microdata, aggregated indicator, or unknown with explanation.
- [ ] At least one variable definition grounded in documentation.
- [ ] One limitation or stewardship risk.
- [ ] AI-use note explaining what was drafted and how it was checked.

## Submission

Submit your completed card in Canvas under the Week 1 module. Starting in Week 2, keep a copy in your course repository as `data-intake-card.md`.

## Scoring Guide

- **Complete:** Stable source, publisher, terms, data level, documented variable definition, limitation/stewardship note, and AI-use note are present.
- **Needs work:** Source documentation is missing, license/terms are unclear, variable definitions are guessed, or limitations are absent.

## Reproducibility Check

- The dataset link is stable or includes an access date.
- The publisher and license are named.
- Variable definitions come from source documentation, not AI guesses.
- The AI-use note states how the student checked AI-assisted text.
